Render this file from the `problem_set_5` folder. The bar chart matches `data/question_2_bar_CORRECTED.png`: boroughs in ascending order of children with BLL greater than 5 mcg/dL.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(kableExtra)
```

\newpage

## Part 1

### Question 1

Load both sheets of `data/two_data_sheets.xlsx`. Sheet 1 is rat maze times. Sheet 2 is home visits.

```{r}
rats <- read_excel("data/two_data_sheets.xlsx", sheet = 1)
visits <- read_excel("data/two_data_sheets.xlsx", sheet = 2)

head(rats)
head(visits)
```

\newpage

### Question 2

#### 2A

Pivot the rat data from wide to long. Columns 1, 2, and 3 are the amount of cheese. Those names become a `cheese` column, and the maze times go in `time`.

```{r}
rats_long <- rats %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("1", "2", "3"),
    names_to = "cheese",
    values_to = "time"
  )
```

#### 2B

```{r}
head(rats_long)
```

\newpage

### Question 3

Mean and standard deviation of maze time for each amount of cheese.

```{r}
rats_long %>%
  group_by(cheese) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_time = mean(time),
    sd_time = sd(time),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

\newpage

### Question 4

#### 4A

Pivot the home visits from long to wide. Each value of `action` becomes its own column, filled with `count`.

```{r}
visits_wide <- visits %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = action,
    values_from = count
  )
```

#### 4B

```{r}
visits_wide
```

\newpage

## Part 2

```{r loading, include=FALSE}
file_path <- "data/Children_Under_6_yrs_with_Elevated_Blood_Lead_Levels__BLL_.csv"
bll_nyc <- read_csv(file_path) %>% drop_na()
colnames(bll_nyc) <- c("borough_id", "time_period",
                       "bll_5", "bll_10", "bll_15", "total_tested")
```

### Question 5

Recreate the 2015-2016 BLL rate table. Several rows share a borough and year, so the counts have to be summed before the rate is calculated.

#### 5A

Filter to 2015-2016 and label the boroughs. Making borough a factor keeps the table in the order 1-5.

```{r}
bll_1516 <- bll_nyc %>%
  filter(time_period %in% c(2015, 2016)) %>%
  mutate(borough = factor(
    borough_id,
    levels = 1:5,
    labels = c("Bronx", "Brooklyn", "Manhattan", "Queens", "Staten Island")
  ))
```

#### 5B

Total children tested, and totals with BLL greater than 5, 10, and 15 mcg/dL, by borough and year.

```{r}
bll_1516 <- bll_1516 %>%
  group_by(borough, time_period) %>%
  summarize(
    bll_5 = sum(bll_5),
    bll_10 = sum(bll_10),
    bll_15 = sum(bll_15),
    total_tested = sum(total_tested),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

#### 5C

Rate per 1,000 tested.

```{r}
bll_1516 <- bll_1516 %>%
  mutate(
    rate_5 = bll_5 / total_tested * 1000,
    rate_10 = bll_10 / total_tested * 1000,
    rate_15 = bll_15 / total_tested * 1000
  )
```

#### 5D

```{r}
bll_1516 %>%
  select(borough, time_period, rate_5, rate_10, rate_15) %>%
  kable(
    digits = 1,
    booktabs = TRUE,
    caption = "BLL Rates per 1,000 tested in New York City, 2015-2016",
    col.names = c("Borough", "Year",
                  "BLL >5 mcg/dL", "BLL >10 mcg/dL", "BLL >15 mcg/dL")
  ) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

\newpage

### Question 6

The bar chart uses the full 2005-2016 file, not the 2015-2016 subset. Boroughs run from the smallest total to the largest.

#### 6A

```{r}
bll_bar <- bll_nyc %>%
  mutate(borough = factor(
    borough_id,
    levels = 1:5,
    labels = c("Bronx", "Brooklyn", "Manhattan", "Queens", "Staten Island")
  )) %>%
  group_by(borough) %>%
  summarize(bll_5 = sum(bll_5), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(borough = fct_reorder(borough, bll_5))

bll_bar
```

#### 6B

```{r}
ggplot(bll_bar, aes(x = borough, y = bll_5)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#ff6600", color = "#003884") +
  labs(
    title = "New York City: Elevated Blood Lead Levels 2005-2016 by Borough",
    x = "boroughs",
    y = "counts of BLL > 5 mcg/dL"
  )
```

The ascending order is Staten Island, Manhattan, Bronx, Queens, Brooklyn.
